questions.stem: A secondary immune response is faster mainly because the first exposure produced:
options: Memory lymphocytes
Fewer antigen receptors
Permanent fever
More skin
questions.explanation: Memory B and T cells persist after the primary response and expand rapidly when the same antigen returns.

questions.stem: A dendritic cell displays an extracellular pathogen-derived peptide on MHC class II. Which cell is activated most directly?
options: Red blood cell
Helper T cell
Platelet
Skeletal muscle cell
questions.explanation: CD4 helper T cells recognize antigen presented on MHC class II and coordinate adaptive immune responses.

questions.stem: A vaccine protects without causing the full disease primarily by:
options: Eliminating all white blood cells
Preventing every mutation
Generating antigen-specific memory
Replacing innate immunity
questions.explanation: Vaccination exposes the immune system to safe antigenic material, producing memory cells that support a stronger later response.

questions.stem: Which feature best distinguishes innate immunity from adaptive immunity?
options: It always improves after each exposure
It is absent at birth
It depends only on antibodies
It responds rapidly through broadly recognizing mechanisms
questions.explanation: Innate defences act rapidly and recognize broad danger patterns. Adaptive responses are antigen-specific and generate stronger memory.

questions.stem: Intact keratinized skin covers the body surface. Which outcome follows most directly?
options: Many pathogens are prevented from entering tissues
The bacterium becomes enclosed and digested
Local blood flow and capillary permeability increase
The antibody binds that antigen selectively
questions.explanation: Many pathogens are prevented from entering tissues. Tightly joined cells, dryness and antimicrobial secretions create a physical and chemical barrier.
